Subject: Follow-up: model fit & multilingual evals (Aurelia Bank)

Hi Lena / Kenji —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + auto-responses in DE/FR/IT for online banking queries.
- Volume: ~120k monthly queries initially, peak season +50%.
- Quality goal: match current triage accuracy ~88% for DE/FR, and >=80% for JA (pilot coverage for APAC ops).
- Constraints: EU data residency for PII, and scoped set of prompts for regulatory review.

Next steps I promised:
1) Recommend a short-list of models to evaluate for accuracy/latency/cost across EU languages.
2) Share our recommended prompt set and initial benchmark results.
3) Agree on sample data to run the live evals (pseudonymized).
4) Schedule a 45-min technical eval run with Rishi & Neha (we can do a screen share).

Model recommendations (initial):
- redwood-mt-large (best balance of cost/quality for DE/FR/IT)
- redwood-mt-xl-q4 (for higher-quality/latency-tolerant flows)
- smaller distilled variant (for high-throughput routing & fallback)

Attachments: I attached the initial prompt set (aurelia_prompt_set_v1.csv) and a short PDF of our EU/APAC benchmark summaries (redwood-eval-benchmarks-eu-apac.pdf).

Can you: (a) confirm which languages you want included in the pilot (I noted DE/FR/IT + JA), and (b) share any sample anonymized transcripts (or a pointer to a secure S3 link) by EoD Wednesday so we can kick off the runs?

If that works, I'll loop in Rishi to propose an eval plan and timeline.

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming: DE/FR/IT are high priority, JA is optional for phase 1 but we'd like a short feasibility check.

A couple items from our side:
- Data: we can provide a pseudonymized export (~5k rows) for pilot. I'll work with our security team and share a secure SFTP link by EoD Friday.

Forwarding Lena's reply. Key asks we should cover in the pilot: EU-only processing, KMS options, p95 latency targets (200ms ideal), and per-language quality breakdowns for redwood-mt-large vs mt-xl.

Proposed internal plan:
1) Run token-level benchmarks on the redwood eval infra against the attached prompt set for DE/FR/IT (and a small JA subset). Use both redwood-mt-large and redwood-mt-xl-q4.
2) Produce per-language precision/recall metrics and a short error analysis for banking-specific intents (account balance, payments, fraud reports).
3) Run a latency profile in our EU region (Frankfurt) with 1-2k concurrent short requests to estimate p95.
4) Produce a recommended routing policy: default to mt-large, fall back to distill for high-throughput non-sensitive flows; route sensitive PII flows to dedicated capacity with KMS.

Attachments referenced earlier: aurelia_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood-eval-benchmarks-eu-apac.pdf. I'll ask Rishi to scope the eval run and timeline (2-3 business days once we get sample data).
